newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian barracks blast kills 11 cadets.
newsitem.headline: Russian barracks blast kills 11 cadets.

text.p: Eleven young cadets were killed at a Russian military academy and 37 were injured when their slum-like barracks collapsed in the west Siberian town of Tomsk on Thursday.

An Emergencies Ministry spokeswoman said nearly 150 people, mostly cadets, were in a three-storey 19th-century monastery taken over by the military in early 1950s but never repaired since then. The roof caved in five minutes before reveille.
The spokeswoman said the number of victims could have been much more if many cadets had not been playing truant that night.
"The ones who went AWOL were the lucky ones," she added.
Trained Emergency Ministry rescue teams were rushed to Tomsk from other regions. Minister Sergei Shoigu headed the operation.
Russian radio and television announced emergency telephone numbers on which relatives could get information.
The spokeswoman said rescue work at the Tomsk Military Signals School started four minutes after the accident and was completed by 10 pm (1200 GMT).
"Thirty seven injured have been taken to hospital including 10 in the serious condition," she said. "No one is left alive or dead trapped in the rubble."
Interfax news agency said the Defence Ministry set up a commission to investigate the accident but there was little doubt it had been caused by the poor repair of the building.
Russia's vast network of military academies has deteriorated considerably following the general decline of the Russian armed forces.

President Boris Yeltsin this week ordered a radical military reform which would shrink the army but make it more effective and cost efficient. Cutting the number of military academies is a part of the planned reform.
